newsitem.title: USA: Clinton telephones leaders of Israel, PLO.
newsitem.headline: Clinton telephones leaders of Israel, PLO.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Sunday called Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat to encourage them to do everything possible to resolve their outstanding issues, White House spokesman Mike McCurry told reporters.

McCurry said Clinton had spoken to each leader for about 10 minutes to "encourage them to do everything they can to address the remaining issues relating to Oslo implementation and specifically security related issues and the withdrawal from Hebron."
McCurry said that U.S. special envoy Dennis Ross would shortly be meeting with Arafat to discuss the Middle East peace process.

Asked why Clinton had taken the trouble to call both Arafat and Netanyahu, McCurry said: "They're down to some difficult issues ... the issues are difficult because the concerns on both sids are deeply held."
In Israel, Ross has been trying to fashion a Israeli-PLO deal on the volatile West Bank town of Hebron. He met Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
"It's clear that we have further narrowed the differences that exist but we have not overcome those differences," Ross told reporters after meeting Netanyahu in northern Israel.

Israel's former Labour government agreed over a year ago to redeploy troops away from Hebron, home to 100,000 Palestinians and 400 Jewish settlers, but delayed the pullout after suicide bombings by Moslem militants killed 59 people in Israel in February and March.

Israeli and Palestinian negotiators have been trying to clinch a Hebron deal in nearly three weeks of U.S.-brokered talks. Netanyahu said this week an agreement was close but accused Arafat of procrastinating.
